researched_by: desk research from Forestry England's own pages
policy_summary: National 'Forest Campervan Road Trip' scheme across seven forest car parks, one of which is Kielder in Northumberland. Kielder Castle is the exception to most rules: no pre-booking, park and pay on arrival. Overnight campervan or motorhome stays are NOT permitted in any other Forestry England car park. A single national policy covering hundreds of sites - far less work than a council, and exactly why the landowner tier is tractable.

national_scheme.name: Forest Campervan Road Trip
national_scheme.season_2026: 16 July to 14 September, bookings opened 21 May
national_scheme.price: GBP16/night, GBP14 members; Kielder Castle GBP15 for all

sites.name: Kielder Castle Car Park

sites.notes: First come first served, no pre-booking - the only site in the national scheme without it. Park up after 5pm. Dark sky location. Charges apply to Forestry England members too; overnight is not covered by the free member parking benefit.

sites.name: Elf Kirk Viewpoint, Kielder
sites.notes: Approved for overnight campervan stays by Forestry England and Northumbrian Water jointly. Coin-only on site: ten pound coins, and there is no cash machine in Kielder - the nearest are in Bellingham. Pay by card at Kielder Castle instead, ten miles away, if you have not got the coins.
sites.price_note: Payable at Elf Kirk in GBP1 coins only - ten of them - or by card at Kielder Castle, which is about ten miles away.
sites.geocode_precision: dark-sky site listing with exact coordinates

sites.name: Forestry England Camping - national campsite network
sites.price_note: From GBP13.60 a night at Fineshade Wood to GBP28.60 in the New Forest high season, quoted for two adults and two children. Forestry England members take 10 per cent off all camping bookings.
sites.notes:
THE BIG GAP IN THE 2026-07-26 FILE. Forestry England does not only tolerate campervans in seven car parks for two months a year - it owns and sells a fourteen-campsite touring business, all of it invisible from the car park and campervan-stopover pages that the first pass worked from.

Ownership resolved. Camping in the Forest was a joint venture with The Camping and Caravanning Club. Forestry England and Forestry and Land Scotland bought a 72 per cent controlling shareholding from the Club, the Club ran the sites through a transition year in 2022, and the two national forestry bodies then took their own countries' sites separately. In 2026 the Club has no operating role in England: the brand is Forestry England Camping, the member discount is Forestry England's, and the Camping in the Forest name has gone from Forestry England's own pages.

The estate is fourteen campsites in five clusters. Ten in the New Forest, run under contract by Camping New Forest (see the separate record). Four elsewhere - Sherwood Pines, Bracelands in the Forest of Dean, Rendlesham in Suffolk and Fineshade Wood in Northamptonshire - branded Forestry England Camping and each booked through its own single-site company and domain (sherwoodpinescamping.co.uk, bracelandscamping.co.uk, rendleshamcamping.co.uk, fineshadecampsite.co.uk). All four take motorhomes, campervans and caravans; hardstanding and electric hook-up are normal.

Separately, Forest Holidays is a public-private partnership founded by the Forestry Commission in 1973, letting woodland cabins on leased Forestry England land; Forest Holidays announced in its own news pages that Sykes Holiday Cottages has acquired it, and Forestry England describes the arrangement only as 'a unique public private partnership'. Cabins only - no touring pitches - so it is out of scope for this dataset, but it is the reason a search for Forestry England accommodation returns cabin prices rather than pitch prices.

This file records the network plus six of the fourteen campsites individually. The other eight are the New Forest sites other than Setthorns and Holmsley; they are named in the Camping New Forest record but not pinned, because no postcode or coordinate was published for them.

sites.name: Sherwood Pines Campsite, Nottinghamshire
sites.price_note: Listed from GBP22 a night on campsites.co.uk for 2026. Three touring tiers - powered grass, hardstanding with electric, and fully serviced with water and drainage. Forestry England members 10 per cent off.
sites.search_hint: Sherwood Pines Campsite, Kings Clipstone, Mansfield
sites.notes: Forestry England's flagship campsite, opened 2021, 20 acres inside Sherwood Pines forest park. Open all year. Booking limited to 21 consecutive nights. The operational detail that matters to a late-running van: the barriers are locked at 22:30 and arrivals after that are refused, so this is not a site to aim at after a long drive. Grass, hardstanding and fully serviced pitches for motorhomes, campervans and caravans, plus tent pitches and glamping bothies. Pitchup reports roughly 425 pitches across all types; Forestry England publishes no count, so treat that as indicative.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid; Pitchup independently gives 53.16369 / -1.09429 for the same site, about 150m away, so the pin is on the campsite rather than the wider forest park

sites.name: Bracelands Campsite, Forest of Dean
sites.price_note: Listed from GBP18 a night on campsites.co.uk for 2026. Midweek discounts, three nights for the price of two, group and seasonal rates. Forestry England members 10 per cent off.
sites.notes: Open all year, caravan and motorhome pitches alongside camping, glamping pods and summer safari tents. Forestry England's own page for the site also advertises campervan stopovers here, which is the only place the stopover scheme and the campsite business appear on the same page anywhere in the estate. Single-night bookings accepted, which is unusual for a full campsite and makes it usable as a touring stop.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid (Bracelands Drive, Berry Hill); not corroborated against a second coordinate source, so the pin may be a few hundred metres from the entrance

sites.name: Rendlesham Campsite, Suffolk
sites.price_note: Not published on Forestry England's page; booked through rendleshamcamping.co.uk. Forestry England members 10 per cent off.
sites.notes: Ninety mixed grass and hardstanding pitches over ten acres for caravans, motorhomes, campervans and tents. Open April to December, so not a winter option. Has a waste disposal point, which matters more than the trail network to anyone touring. Tangham is the old Forestry Commission site by the Rendlesham Forest UFO trail.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid (Tangham, Rendlesham Forest); single-source

sites.name: Fineshade Wood Campsite, Northamptonshire
sites.price_note: 'Pitches start from just GBP13.60 per night' - Forestry England, 2026. The cheapest published pitch price in the Forestry England estate. Members 10 per cent off.
sites.search_hint: Fineshade Wood campsite, Top Lodge, near Corby
sites.notes: Hardstanding plots for motorhomes and caravans on the edge of Fineshade Wood, off the A43 between Stamford and Corby. Marketed on dark skies. Booked through fineshadecampsite.co.uk. Season and pitch count are not published; the price is.
sites.geocode_precision: Top Lodge, Fineshade Wood postcode centroid - the visitor centre address rather than the camping field itself

sites.name: Camping New Forest - ten Forestry England campsites in the New Forest
sites.price_note: From GBP16 a night at Setthorns to GBP28.60 at Holmsley, quoted for two adults and two children, 2026.
sites.notes:
The Wansbeck/Ballater pattern, at scale. Forestry England owns the land and the campsites; Camping New Forest runs them under contract - 'We're delighted to have been chosen to run Forestry England's ten New Forest campsites'. Camping New Forest is part of The New Forest Agricultural Show Society, company number 14159381, which already ran Long Meadow before taking the Forestry England contract. Forestry England's own page calls them 'our partners'. These are therefore Forestry England records, with the operator named, not Camping and Caravanning Club records.

The ten: Ashurst, Ocknell, Roundhill, Longbeech (adults only), Long Meadow, Hollands Wood, Setthorns, Holmsley, Aldridge Hill, Matley Wood and Denny Wood - eleven names appear across the operator's pages because Long Meadow is counted alongside the ten Forestry England sites, and Denny Wood reopened in 2026 after closure.

All of them take motorhomes and campervans. Facilities split sharply: Ashurst, Ocknell, Roundhill, Long Meadow, Hollands Wood and Holmsley have toilets and showers; Longbeech, Setthorns, Aldridge Hill, Matley Wood and Denny Wood have none at all and require you to carry your own toilet. Several have no electric hook-up but do have battery charging. Gates open 07:30 and lock 22:00 across the estate.

Only Setthorns and Holmsley are pinned individually below. The other eight publish no postcode or coordinates on the operator's site and are not mapped here rather than guessed.

sites.name: Setthorns Campsite, New Forest
sites.price_note: From GBP16.00 a night for two adults and two children, 2026.
sites.self_contained_definition: no toilets or showers on site at all - the operator requires guests to bring a chemical toilet; a chemical disposal point and drinking water taps are provided
sites.search_hint: Setthorns Campsite, near Sway, New Forest
sites.notes: The one Forestry England New Forest site open all year, and the obvious motorhome choice in the cluster: hardstanding and XL pitches, electric hook-up, chemical disposal, and no toilet block to pay for. Gates open 07:30 and are locked at 22:00, so arrival is bounded. Minimum three nights over bank holiday weekends and two nights over summer school-holiday weekends. Mobile signal is poor - relevant if you intend to book or pay on arrival.
sites.geocode_precision: operator's published address postcode centroid; the campsite is a long strip along a forest track, so the pin is within the site's area but not on a specific entrance

sites.name: Holmsley Campsite, New Forest
sites.price_note: From GBP28.60 a night for two adults and two children, 2026 - the most expensive pitch found anywhere in the Forestry England estate.
sites.notes: Hardstanding, grass and XL pitches on part of the WWII Holmsley airfield; open 26 March to 2 November 2026. Electric pitches are allocated on arrival rather than chosen, which is worth knowing if you need a particular length. Gates open 07:30, locked 22:00. Minimum three nights over bank holiday weekends, two over summer school-holiday weekends.
sites.geocode_precision: operator's published address postcode centroid on Forest Road; the site occupies part of the former airfield and the entrance may be several hundred metres from the pin. Single-source - worth checking on the ground

notes: Kielder Castle is due to reopen in summer 2026 after redevelopment, coinciding with Kielder Forest's centenary. Overnight parking has continued during the works.
provision_sweep_2026_07_27: Gap-filling sweep for provision the car park pages do not mention (research protocol step 2). Result: large. Forestry England runs a fourteen-campsite touring business - ten New Forest sites operated under contract by Camping New Forest, plus Sherwood Pines, Bracelands, Rendlesham and Fineshade Wood under the Forestry England Camping brand - none of which is reachable from the campervan-stopover or car park pages the first pass used. Camping in the Forest is finished as an English brand: Forestry England and Forestry and Land Scotland bought 72 per cent from The Camping and Caravanning Club, the Club operated a transition year in 2022, and the Club has no role now. Forest Holidays cabins were checked and excluded - leased land, cabins only, no touring pitches. Six of the fourteen campsites are pinned here; the other eight are the New Forest sites that publish no postcode.
open_questions: Prices are published inconsistently. Fineshade quotes GBP13.60, Setthorns GBP16 and Holmsley GBP28.60 on operator pages; Sherwood Pines and Bracelands prices here come from campsites.co.uk listings rather than the operators. Pitch-type and season breakdowns need pulling from each booking engine.
Pitch counts exist only for Rendlesham (90). Sherwood Pines is reported at about 425 pitches by Pitchup and publishes nothing itself. The other twelve publish nothing.

Eight of the ten New Forest campsites are unmapped because Camping New Forest publishes no postcodes or coordinates for them - Ashurst, Ocknell, Roundhill, Longbeech, Long Meadow, Hollands Wood, Aldridge Hill, Matley Wood and Denny Wood. Ordnance Survey or park4night would settle them.

Camping in the Forest formerly had sites at Cannock Chase and Delamere among others. Neither appears anywhere in Forestry England's 2026 camping offer. Whether they closed, were let to a separate operator, or were sold was not established.
Is the maximum stay of 21 consecutive nights at Sherwood Pines a network rule or a site rule? No other site publishes a maximum.
Does the ownership change alter anything for Camping and Caravanning Club members? The Club's own discounts and the Forestry England member discount are now different schemes on the same sites.

Forest Holidays announces on its own site that it has been acquired by Sykes Holiday Cottages; neither the date nor Forestry England's residual shareholding was established, and neither Forestry England nor Forest Holidays publishes the lease terms over Forestry England land. It would matter if Forest Holidays ever added touring pitches.
